doc.title: Ada Rovatti interviewed by Monk Rowe, via Zoom, December 13, 2022

title: Italy, America and politics
summary: She describes being shocked by American politics and racism and notes Italy's own problems.

story.theme_name: Race and segregation in the jazz life
story.community_name: Politics, race and the state of the country

blocks.x: Yeah we had said that earlier that we can do this, but should we? You can pass on this question if you’d like but it’s not a music question but I’m curious when people like yourself relocate to the United States and observe our political and social issues what do you think about it?

Oy. That’s the answer right there. Well especially from Italy where it’s well known to have a messed up political situation, nothing stands more than a couple of months. We had from Berlusconi to a porn star in the politic world, I don’t know if you know a few

years ago. So we had really like a lot of buffoon and circus character. Coming here, and if I am shocked — I was shocked to see what was happening here politically that tells you a lot. I think that all the world was pretty shocked to see — I mean I’m pretty open about my political view. I’m definitely not a Trumpist, let’s put it like that. And I was totally shocked that the country like the United States — you see I grew up and I know that all my fellow European or all over the world, we always grew up looking at the United States like the best of the best. They have the best music, the best movies, the best everything was just like portrayed. We grew up looking at the American movies — it gave us an idea of the American lifestyle so we always looked up. And then coming here and see all these kind of like different sided I guess was always hidden under the rock but then suddenly it came out with the political — you know we didn’t growing up there was never showing about racism in a certain way. You saw it as maybe something in the past — maybe like but not something that when I moved here I was shocked about the poverty, all the problems of a beautiful country because I’m going to be always thankful about this country, welcomed me and I had a lot of opportunity. But there was a lot of things that unfortunately just in the last few years they really came out under the rock really. A lot of hatred, racism, you know. So it’s kind of sad and hopefully we’ll be more and more recognized and put under the lights and just do something about it. I think yes a lot of it was done from the last hundred years but there is still a lot to go you know. And the way when I was raised in Italy we didn’t have a vision of America like that. Definitely.
Well we probably have an incorrect vision of Italy because we see in ads and in tours, you know take a tour of the best parts of Italy. So if we were to relocate to somewhere in Italy we probably —

Yeah. Every country sees the downside. Of course we want to portray the best of us. It’s like when you go on a date app — you want to put your best picture and your best characteristics. You know? So I think every country — I mean we have — right now we have a very bad economical situation. Kind of similar to what it was here a few years — a couple of years ago with the Republican — not Republican, we’ll say with Trump. But so right now, you know we have a lot of poverty and unfortunately we have also a lot of racists now, one thing that was pretty new to Italy. Because when I grew up okay we didn’t have so much of a multi-cultural life. But every time I go back it’s a lot of things change and didn’t change for the best unfortunately.
